author: w360
scope: Exact finite-box reduction for bounded positive edge weights
exact_statement: For edge weights in [1,2] on nearest-neighbor undirected Z^2, integer n>=1, T(0,n e1) is the minimum over simple paths inside [-2n,2n]^2, and n<=T<=2n.
reproduction: The n-edge horizontal path costs at most 2n. Every path needs at least n edges and costs at least n. Any path leaving the indicated box must have at least 2n+1 edges before its first outside vertex and therefore costs greater than 2n. Positive loops can be removed. The finite graph has finitely many simple contenders, so its minimum exists and equals the full-lattice infimum. Iid and continuity are unnecessary for this deterministic lemma.
remaining_gap: This reduction gives no n^(2/3) variance law, curvature, or KPZ relation. Review of any later w360 proof steps remains pending.
